posts.cooked:
@Everyone,

I wasn't there all the time (RPGs to play, stuff to buy and computers to build) but I had a hell of a time. I got to demo a lot of the new villains, beat my nemesis (Voss) and had a heck of a time. I'd like to thank Evandan for letting me and my friend get in on the game mid fight between us and Plague Rat when Dakota had to leave. Everything was pretty sweet when I got Unity rolling in high fashion and had enough DPS to chew through (Litterally) everything that got in the way and then some. Cheers to all and hopefully I'll be getting the upgrade for the original bos here within the next week so i can store all my SoTM in one box and be able to get more people to play.

One thing I'm just going to throw out there is that I want to play with people but distance (I live in Kansas) and time (I work a lot) seem to hold me back from getting any games in with people I know around here (most of which expressed amazingly negative interest in playing SoTM.) So if anyone wants to play over skype sometime, just PM and I'll give you my skype name. I have a webcam, mic and such so a laptop would make it like I was already there and such.

- Sim (The guy wearing the Chicago White Sox hat)

posts.name: Hank34
posts.cooked:
@ Ronway

I went to GenCon specifically for the chance to get the Enhanced Edition.  It is the only reason I went to GenCon.  I am not really big on playing games with strangers, or large sweaty crowds for that matter.  It was also my first Con experience ever.

I have been wanting Sentinels of the Multiverse for a long time now, and every time I go into my FLGS, the 1st edition sits there, mocking me.  I have held off longer than I can remember buying the 1st edition, soley because I knew the Enhanced Edition would be coming out. 

No one said anything about kickstarters.  As they FUNDED the new expansion, they are entitled to have their games first.  As for the common slob that sits in his bathrobe ordering games from the online store, yes I feel that my order should have precedence over theirs.  If I had known that my order would be lumped in with the regular internet folk, I would have never made the trip out to Indy in the first place. 

I also didn't claim to be "better" than anyone so don't know where that came from.  Great advice though that I should be directing my anger at the wind instead of the company from which I bought the product. 

The good news is that my "anger", if you can call it that, will be fixed when I get my games.  I'm hoping that it will arrive next week (week 6).  Can you really blame me for wanting to play this awesome game?
